data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding were GBP 180.1m. The claims development triangle indicates a net adverse prior-year development of approximately GBP 26.0m (around 14.4% of opening gross reserves), driven largely by deterioration in certain older underwriting years (notably a material movement in 2015 development). The report highlights large natural catastrophe activity in 2017 (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, California wildfires, Mexico earthquakes) which affected the 2017 year of account and market loss environment; prior-year adverse development appears to be driven by large loss/claim development rather than a single change in reserving methodology. The gross prior-year movement figure above is derived from the gross claims development table.
raw_causal_phrases: the worst year for catastrophes in the US for over a decade with Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, the wildfires in California and earthquakes in Mexico causing insured market losses of $135 billion the costliest year on record (source: Munich Re).
The impact of the catastrophe losses on Syndicate 1910 net of reinsurance recoveries added 18.16 percentage points to the combined ratio.
The 2016 Year of Account has performed creditably given that it was affected by Hurricane Matthew and fires in Alberta.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development amount is calculated from the gross claims development triangle (claims development table) because the report does not provide a single explicit gross 'movement in prior year's provision' aggregate. The triangle extraction required aligning staggered rows; there is moderate uncertainty in the precise prior-year movement (confidence 0.8). No explicit gross PY movement figure was provided in a dedicated movement note. Some narrative figures quoted in the report are net of reinsurance and were not used for the gross PY movement.
